text:
pete: Weird onboarding quirk: I `redwoodctl login --profile pete-work` and browser auth succeeds, but my sample app still picks the default profile. CLI `whoami` shows me logged in as pete-work. Any ideas?

hana: did you set REDWOOD_PROFILE or REDWOOD_CONFIG in your env? sample app reads env first.

pete: nope. No env var. I see two profiles in ~/.config/redwood/config.yaml: `default` and `pete-work` where pete-work is the one I logged into. I used `redwoodctl login --profile pete-work --no-open` to test headless.

sylvie: can you paste the sample-app startup log? It should print which profile it loaded.

pete: log excerpt:
```
INFO  sample-app: using profile "default" (loaded from ~/.config/redwood/config.yaml)
WARN  sample-app: token expired for profile default, attempting refresh
ERROR sample-app: refresh failed, falling back to unauthenticated
```

pete: but `redwoodctl whoami --profile pete-work` shows my user.

hana: two hypotheses: (A) sample-app resolves profile names to IDs and we have an alias collision where `default` and `pete-work` share the same internal id (happened once when importing org demo configs), or (B) redwoodctl login currently writes the token to a file path keyed by profile *label*, but sample-app expects the token file keyed by profile *id*, so they mismatch. Which version of redwoodctl and sample-app?

pete: redwoodctl 0.37.0, sample-app v1.2.3 (dev image).

sylvie: that version of sample-app changed to prefer profile IDs because we had profile rename bugs. There's a parity mismatch here. Dev image might have an older runtime pinned.

pete: aargh. So install mismatch again. Any quick workaround so I can demo?

hana: brute force: copy the token file from the pete-work token path to the default token path. `cp ~/.config/redwood/tokens/pete-work.cache ~/.config/redwood/tokens/default.cache` then restart sample-app. That should make it read the token it expects. Not ideal but works for a demo.

pete: did that, sample-app now shows me as pete-work. Thanks.

sylvie: long term: we need (1) a compatibility shim in the SDK so both label and id keyed stores are checked, (2) a doctor check that warns when multiple components have mismatched versions (redwoodctl vs sample-app vs SDK), (3) a migration tool that can remap token stores when a component moves to ID-based keys. I'll open an issue.

qa-bot: Created bug QA-9876: "profile token key mismatch between label-keyed redwoodctl tokens and id-keyed runtimes". Attached minimal repro and steps.

pete: another oddity I hit: after forcing login multiple times while testing, redwoodctl started delaying auth retries with backoff that felt really long (like ~2 minutes) before failing. Onboarded devs might wait and think it's broken.

hana: we added exponential backoff to avoid token-service hammering when the auth provider rate-limits. But DX-wise the CLI should surface immediate feedback and allow a `--no-backoff` or `--fast-fail` during interactive onboarding. What did the logs show?

pete: `redwoodctl login --verbose` showed `INFO auth: retrying in 128s` then `INFO auth: retrying in 256s` in some runs — that seems aggressive for localdev.

sylvie: agreed. Let's change default backoff ceiling for interactive sessions to something like 8s with jitter, and keep aggressive backoff only for non-interactive batch/CI mode. Also add `REDWOOD_CLI_BACKOFF=interactive` override and a `--no-backoff` flag for troubleshooting.

hana: action items: (A) add a CLI flag `--no-backoff` and an env var to control interactive vs CI backoff heuristic, (B) detect interactive tty and use a friendlier retry schedule, (C) print a helpful message when backoff is active like "Retrying auth in 5s (use --no-backoff to fail fast during testing)".

infra: please also add a check in our packaging pipeline to ensure we don't ship incompatible SDK/runtime versions together in the dev images. This keeps sample-app and redwoodctl parity tighter.

pete: one more small DX bug: `redwoodctl login --profile` sometimes ignores the flag if REDWOOD_PROFILE env var is set; it should at least warn that env overrides CLI flag. I lost time wondering why my flag was ignored.

hana: yep we had a policy: env vars override flags for CI reproducibility, but interactive CLI should warn when flags are suppressed by env. Add to action items.

sylvie: I'll consolidate into a single ticket: compatibility shim, doctor checks for version mismatch and env/flag conflicts, backoff config, and clearer login messages. devex-bot: Created issue #5422: "DX: profile key parity + backoff/flag ergonomics + doctor checks" and added labels: devex, onboarding, sdk-parity.

pete: thanks all — got my demo working. I'll paste the ad-hoc steps I used so docs can include a troubleshooting snippet. Marking resolved for now.

hana: thanks for reporting — useful combo of issues. We'll try to land low-risk triage patches this sprint. :thumbsup:
